hero.title: Jumu'ah Mubarak
hero.sub: The best day of the week

sunnahs.title: Take a bath (Ghusl)
sunnahs.note: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever performs Ghusl on Friday and then goes to the mosque, it is an expiation for him until the next Friday."

sunnahs.title: Wear your best clothes
sunnahs.note: It is a day of gathering — present yourself beautifully before Allah. Clean clothes are a sign of respect for the occasion.

sunnahs.title: Use Siwak / clean your teeth
sunnahs.note: The Prophet ﷺ encouraged the Siwak on Fridays especially. Cleanliness of the mouth is part of the sunnah of the day.

sunnahs.title: Apply perfume (men)
sunnahs.note: For men attending the mosque, perfume is recommended on Friday. Women should not wear perfume when going out to the masjid.

sunnahs.title: Go early to the masjid
sunnahs.note: The earlier you go, the greater the reward. The angels sit at the door of the mosque recording each arrival in order.

sunnahs.title: Recite Surah Al-Kahf
sunnahs.sub: A light between the two Fridays
sunnahs.note: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever recites Surah Al-Kahf on Friday, a light will shine for him between the two Fridays." (al-Hakim)

sunnahs.title: Send abundant salawat
sunnahs.sub: Presented to the Prophet ﷺ on Friday
sunnahs.note: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Send abundant salawat upon me on Friday, for it is presented to me." (Abu Dawud)

duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَىٰ نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ
duas.translit: Allahumma salli wa sallim 'ala nabiyyina Muhammad
duas.en: O Allah, send prayers and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad.

duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَغِثْنَا، اللَّهُمَّ أَغِثْنَا، اللَّهُمَّ أَغِثْنَا
duas.translit: Allahumma aghithna, Allahumma aghithna, Allahumma aghithna
duas.en: O Allah, send us rain. O Allah, send us rain. O Allah, send us rain.
duas.ref: The Prophet ﷺ sought rain on this day

duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ عَفُوٌّ تُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ فَاعْفُ عَنِّي
duas.en: O Allah, You are Most Forgiving, and You love forgiveness; so forgive me.
duas.ref: Recite frequently — especially in the last hour before Maghrib

duas.arabic: لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
duas.translit: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa Huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir
duas.en: There is no god but Allah alone, He has no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is Able to do all things.
duas.ref: A treasure — recite 10× in the morning and evening

duaHourNote: There is an hour on Friday when no Muslim asks Allah for anything except that He grants it. Many scholars say it is the last hour before Maghrib — so make dua between Asr and Maghrib.
khutbahEtiquette: Stay silent during the khutbah — even telling someone to be quiet breaks it.
Do not step over people to reach a seat.
Sit close to the imam if there is space.
Listen attentively — no phone, no conversation.
If you arrive during the khutbah, sit at the nearest place and listen.
khutbahNote: The khutbah is not a lecture — it is a reminder. Treat it as an act of worship.
